Beta intervention guide

Operator steps for a governed Beta run: inspect the exact proposal, reject stale intent, approve as a distinct person, resume, export evidence, and replay without another mutation.

OperatorDeveloperEvaluatorRunbookBETA
PrerequisitesA reference-profile deployment with PostgreSQL and the background owner loop · An operator token scoped to the project containing the run · The Beta scope and reference-profile pages
Reviewed 2026-11-03 · current main branch docs contract

Use this guide when a governed Beta run stops for a person, when an approval is no longer safe to consume, or when an evidence archive must be inspected. It describes the installed Cookbook 22 journey and the real run-scoped API that the SDK and CLI wrap. The Harborlight case is synthetic: it is a control-flow fixture, not a credit decision and not a claim about model quality.

All HTTP paths below are relative to /ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/caliber. The server derives project and authorization scope from the authenticated identity and run; never add a caller-supplied project to an evidence or approval request.

The intervention decision tree#

State or symptomSafe first actionNever do
waiting_approvalRead the run's approvals, then inspect the exact approval view and proposalApprove from the initiating editor or reconstruct the proposal from input text
Approval is expired, superseded, or already consumedRe-read the approval view and create a new run if the request is still neededRetry an old approval id or edit a stored approval/policy row
Run is approved but still waitingConfirm the approval is bound to the same run and proposal, then use the operator resume actionSend the downstream request directly or click a second approval path
Run is acceptedDownload and verify the evidence archive, then use read-only replay if neededTreat a successful HTTP status as proof of downstream acceptance without the archive/receipt chain
Replay reports matches_original: falseHold the result, compare the recorded observations and criteria version, and open a defect/review itemRe-run the live workflow to make the replay pass
Evidence returns 410 evidence_expiredRetain the tombstone and export metadata; recover from the source run only if policy allows a new exportRecreate an expired archive under the old scope or claim the bytes are recoverable

1. Inspect a run that is waiting for approval#

UI: open Workflows → Runs, select the project, then open the run detail page. The run state must be waiting_approval. The approval panel should show the pending runtime approval id and the project/run scope. For the installed Cookbook 22 journey, the proposal describes one request_missing_document action for case MORT-2026-000184, document pay_statement, expected version 1.

API:

RUN_ID="run-..."
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $CALIBER_TOKEN" \
  "$CALIBER_BASE_URL/ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/caliber/workflow-runs/$RUN_ID" | jq '.data | {workflow_run_id,status,project_id,acceptance}'

curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $CALIBER_TOKEN" \
  "$CALIBER_BASE_URL/ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/caliber/workflow-runs/$RUN_ID/approvals" | jq '.data'

The list response identifies runtime_approval_id. Use that id with the same RUN_ID to read the approval view:

APPROVAL_ID="runtime-approval-..."
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $CALIBER_TOKEN" \
  "$CALIBER_BASE_URL/ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/caliber/workflow-runs/$RUN_ID/approvals/$APPROVAL_ID" \
  | jq '.data | {approval,binding,proposal,policy,quorum,state,allowed_responses,caller}'

The proposal is nested in this view. The current contract has no standalone ProposalsAPI or proposal route. The binding pins the intent/evidence/policy digests and expected resource version; compare them before deciding.

SDK:

approvals = caliber.workflows.runs.approvals(run_id)
runtime_approval_id = approvals[0].runtime_approval_id
view = caliber.workflows.runs.approval(run_id, runtime_approval_id)
assert view.proposal is not None

2. Reject an unsafe or stale approval#

UI: from the approval panel, choose Reject, enter a concise reason that states the evidence or policy mismatch, and confirm. The run must remain scoped to the same project and the approval must still be open. If the UI reports an expired or superseded state, stop and start a new run instead of retrying.

API:

curl -sS -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CALIBER_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"runtime_approval_id":"'"$APPROVAL_ID"'","reason":"the expected resource version is stale"}' \
  "$CALIBER_BASE_URL/ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/caliber/workflow-runs/$RUN_ID/approval/reject" | jq '.data'

SDK:

caliber.workflows.runs.decide(
    run_id,
    runtime_approval_id=runtime_approval_id,
    decision="reject",
    reason="the expected resource version is stale",
)

request_changes can appear in allowed_responses as policy metadata, but it is not an executable decision route in this release. A client must not invent /approval/request-changes.

3. Approve the exact proposal as a distinct person#

UI: sign in as the project approver, not the initiating editor. Re-open the same run and approval, compare the proposal resource and arguments with the request, then choose Approve. A self-approval must display 403 project_role_required and must not create a downstream mutation.

API:

curl -sS -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APPROVER_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"runtime_approval_id":"'"$APPROVAL_ID"'","reason":"the exact synthetic request is authorized"}' \
  "$CALIBER_BASE_URL/ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/caliber/workflow-runs/$RUN_ID/approval/approve" | jq '.data'

SDK:

approved = approver.workflows.runs.decide(
    run_id,
    runtime_approval_id=runtime_approval_id,
    decision="approve",
    reason="the exact synthetic request is authorized",
)

An approval response may be a partial-quorum acknowledgement. It does not resume the run automatically. Check the approval state again and use the operator action only after the required decision is recorded.

4. Resume and verify the accepted outcome#

UI: as the operator, choose Resume on the approved run. Watch the run detail state move through queued or running to completed; the acceptance panel must say accepted. The run must show one governed effect and one receipt. If a connector is unbound or has no authoritative verifier, the run refuses closed before a proposal is created; that is an expected safety result.

API:

curl -sS -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $CALIBER_TOKEN" \
  "$CALIBER_BASE_URL/ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/caliber/workflow-runs/$RUN_ID/resume" | jq '.data'

curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $CALIBER_TOKEN" \
  "$CALIBER_BASE_URL/ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/caliber/workflow-runs/$RUN_ID" \
  | jq '.data | {status,acceptance}'

curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $CALIBER_TOKEN" \
  "$CALIBER_BASE_URL/ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/caliber/workflow-runs/$RUN_ID/causal-links?limit=200" \
  | jq '.data.effects'

The causal links should connect proposal, approval, decision, effect and receipt. A 201 first downstream commit, 200 same-key replay and 412 stale If-Match are downstream fixture assertions, not permission to bypass the dispatcher.

5. Read and verify the evidence package#

UI: on the run detail page choose Evidence → Download. Keep the archive with the run id, package digest and authorization scope. Do not upload it to an unapproved service.

API:

curl -sS -D evidence.headers -o evidence.zip \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CALIBER_TOKEN" \
  "$CALIBER_BASE_URL/ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/caliber/workflow-runs/$RUN_ID/evidence"

The route returns a deterministic ZIP for the server-authorized view. The SDK leaves the bytes available to the server-free archive verifier:

archive = caliber.workflows.runs.evidence(run_id)
assert archive[:2] == b"PK"

An expired archive returns 410 with reason: evidence_expired and a tombstone. Keep that tombstone as evidence of retention enforcement; do not recreate the old archive under the same scope.

6. Replay without another mutation#

UI: choose Evidence → Replay only when the browser journey exposes the replay control. The result is a read-only comparison and must display the server's matches_original value.

CLI:

caliberctl workflow run replay "$RUN_ID"

Exit 0 means matches_original: true; exit 1 means the comparison ran and found a mismatch. A refusal or malformed archive is an API/verification failure, not a match.

API and SDK:

curl -sS -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $CALIBER_TOKEN" \
  "$CALIBER_BASE_URL/ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/caliber/workflow-runs/$RUN_ID/replay" | jq '.data | {workflow_run_id,matches_original,criteria_version,decisions}'
report = caliber.workflows.runs.replay(run_id)
assert report.matches_original

Replay does not call a model, dispatcher, downstream or live provider. A mismatch requires investigation of the pinned manifest, recorded observations and criteria version; starting a new live run is a separate, explicitly reviewed action.

Operational records#

Record the following with every intervention: UTC timestamp, deployment/candidate SHA, project and run id, approval id, proposal id, decision principal and reason, response/error code, evidence archive/package digest, replay result, and whether any downstream mutation was observed. Redact payload values and credentials. The records are evidence of an operator decision, not a replacement for the independent Beta security review or the release decision in #613.
